title: Streaming Journal Slice & Rewrite Protocol for Nested Structured Output
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Nested JSON arrays and objects produced by streaming LLM responses (including interleaved tool calls) frequently get truncated mid-entity. Existing heuristics attempt naive escape or object completion, which leads to incorrect schema, non-idempotent replays, and operator confusion. Goal: design and implement a "journal slice" protocol that makes each emitted chunk self-describing enough to support idempotent resume, safe rewrites of tail slices, and schema-evolution compatibility across partial replays while keeping wire overhead low. Acceptance criteria: 1) client/SDKs can resume from an arbitrary chunk boundary and reconstruct syntactically valid JSON objects or a well-defined fallback (partial object wrapper) without duplicating side-effecting tool calls; 2) server can rewrite last N slices atomically when a late model correction arrives; 3) latency and token-overhead increase <= 6% on typical prompt distributions; 4) integrates with current tool-calling hooks and console tracing so each toolcall retains provenance across retries.
updates: 2025-02-11: Spike complete. Prototype journal slice envelope with fields: seq, slice_type (atomic|partial|correction), schema_version_hint, toolcall_guard (optional), checksum. Implemented micro-benchmarks showing 3.8% token overhead for 8-byte seq + 1-byte type optimizations.

2025-02-14: Design review with PM/Design. Decided against embedding full schema diffs in each slice; use compact schema_version_hint + remote schema cache in SDK/console. Design doc posted: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456789/Streaming+Journal+Design

2025-02-20: Implementation branch opened. Runtime changes to annotate outgoing chunks with journal headers. Initial client-side SDK patch (JS/Python) to stitch slices and detect partial arrays. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894

2025-02-24: Test plan added. Create fuzz harness that simulates network truncation, reorder, and duplicate chunk delivery. Add golden prompts that include nested arrays of toolcall responses and deeply nested objects with repeated keys. Datadog dashboard for test runs: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/streaming-journal-harness

2025-02-28: Edge decision: toolcalls that are split across slices must include an idempotency token and a toolcall_guard slice that marks the boundary. This prevents double-execution on resume. Security review requested for toolcall idempotency tokens cleared by KMS (pending).
notes: Trade-offs: adding per-slice metadata increases token usage but provides strong resume semantics. Alternative of opaque resends would be cheaper but breaks toolcall idempotency. We must coordinate with SDK teams to deploy client-side stitchers before server defaults to strict journal mode. Follow-up: Canary rollout on dedicated with `slice_mode=compatible` flag.
acceptance_tests: Toolcall idempotency harness with external mock tool (no duplicate exec)
Benchmark: p95 latency compared to baseline, token overhead measurement
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flagged opt-in for SDKs and hosted API (2 weeks). Phase 2: canary on Dedicated for small customers (4 weeks). Phase 3: gradual default flip with monitoring on error rates and token overhead.
